newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese dissidents in HK urges Patten for help.
newsitem.headline: Chinese dissidents in HK urges Patten for help.

text.p: Forty Chinese dissidents stranded in Hong Kong urged Governor Chris Patten to help them emigrate to other countries before the territory reverts to China, a human rights group said on Sunday.
Some of the dissidents have threatened to go on hunger strike if there was no response, and one has threatened to commit suicide by setting himself alight, the group said.

"(The) Chinese dissidents urged the governor to take urgent action to get them out," the Information Centre of Human Rights and Democratic Movement in China, a Hong Kong-based human rights group, said in a statement.
The 40 Chinese dissidents who fled China to the territory have not been accepted by western countries, it said.
As they came to Hong Kong illegally, they cannot become permanent residents and can be sent back to China after Britain hands the colony back to China on July 1, the group said.
The dissidents had sent a letter to Patten through a pro-democracy organisation, the statement said.

"Some of the dissidents told our information centre, if the Hong Kong government does not answer them by May 27, they will take action such as hunger strike before Government House," the human rights group said.
One dissident said he would commit suicide by setting himself on fire, the group said.
